note.en: Sharmishtha, reduced to Devayani's waiting-maid, is the daughter of the Danava king Vrishaparvan.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXXXI ('She is Sarmishtha, the daughter of the Asura king Vrishaparvan')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXXXI has Devayani name Sarmishtha the daughter of the Asura king Vrishaparvan.

note.en: Shukra is Vrishaparvan's household priest and threatens to abandon him over Devayani's humiliation.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXXX ('know, O Vrishaparvan, I shall leave thee and thy relatives! Indeed, O king, for this, I can no longer stay with thee!')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXXX records Kavya (Shukra) confronting Vrishaparvan and threatening to leave him and his relatives.

note.en: Vrishaparvan must placate Devayani after his daughter Sharmishtha casts her into a well.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXXX ('for the mal-treatment of my daughter too, know, O Vrishaparvan, I shall leave thee')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXXX has Shukra reproach Vrishaparvan for the mal-treatment of his daughter Devayani.

note.en: Vrishaparvan's Danavas repeatedly kill Kacha while he studies in Shukra's house.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXXX ('because ye slew the Brahmana Kacha, the grandson of Angiras, who was virtuous... while residing in my abode')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXXX has Shukra charge Vrishaparvan's people with slaying the Brahmana Kacha in his abode.

note.en: Yayati keeps Sharmishtha in his gardens at Devayani's direction, and later fathers sons on her.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXXXII ('the monarch, directed by Devayani, established Vrishaparvan's daughter Sarmishtha in a mansion especially erected near the artificial woods of Asokas in his gardens')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXXXII narrates Yayati establishing Vrishaparvan's daughter Sarmishtha in a mansion in his gardens.

note.en: Brihaspati, priest of the gods against the Asuras, is the son of Angiras.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXXVI ('The gods, then, from desire of victory, installed the son of Angiras (Vrihaspati) as their priest')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXXVI identifies Vrihaspati, the gods' installed priest, as the son of Angiras.

note.en: Kacha is Angiras's grandson through Brihaspati.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXXVII ('O grandson of the Rishi Angiras, in conduct and birth, in learning, asceticism and humility, thou shinest most brightly')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXXVII has Devayani address Kacha as the grandson of the Rishi Angiras.

note.en: Hiranyaksha is named the son of Diti, slain by Vishnu in the boar form.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Santi Parva, Section CCCXL ('I shall then slay the son of Diti, named Hiranyaksha, filled with pride of strength')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Santi Parva Section CCCXL has Vishnu name Hiranyaksha the son of Diti whom he will slay as the boar.

note.en: Hiranyakasipu is named the son of Diti, slain by Vishnu in the Man-lion form.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Santi Parva, Section CCCXL ('Assuming the form then of a Man-lion (Narsingha), I shall, for benefiting the deities, slay Hiranyakasipu the son of Diti')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Santi Parva Section CCCXL has Vishnu name Hiranyakasipu the son of Diti whom he will slay as Narasimha.

note.en: Both Hiranyaksha and Hiranyakasipu are named sons of Diti in the same passage.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Santi Parva, Section CCCXL ('I shall then slay the son of Diti, named Hiranyaksha... I shall... slay Hiranyakasipu the son of Diti')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Santi Parva Section CCCXL calls Hiranyaksha and Hiranyakasipu each the son of Diti in consecutive sentences.

note.en: Vishnu, in the boar form, slays Hiranyaksha.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Anusasana Parva, Section CXXVI ('Assuming the form of a boar I slew Hiranyaksha. Assuming the form of a dwarf I conquered (the Asura) king Vali')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Anusasana Parva Section CXXVI has Vishnu himself say he slew Hiranyaksha in the form of a boar.

note.en: The boar incarnation is the form in which Hiranyaksha is killed.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Anusasana Parva, Section CXXVI ('Assuming the form of a boar I slew Hiranyaksha')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Anusasana Parva Section CXXVI attributes Hiranyaksha's death to Vishnu's boar (Varaha) form.

note.en: The Man-lion incarnation is the form in which Hiranyakasipu is killed.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Santi Parva, Section CCCXL ('Assuming the form then of a Man-lion (Narsingha), I shall, for benefiting the deities, slay Hiranyakasipu the son of Diti, who will be a great destroyer of sacrifices')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Santi Parva Section CCCXL has Vishnu declare he will slay Hiranyakasipu assuming the form of a Man-lion.

note.en: Hiranyaksha stands with Virochana in the list of Danava chiefs who overthrew righteousness.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Santi Parva, Section CLXVI ('They were Hiranyakasipu, and Hiranyaksha, and Virochana, and Samvara, and Viprachitti, and Prahlada, and Namuchi, and Vali')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Santi Parva Section CLXVI lists Hiranyaksha and Virochana together among the foremost Danavas who defied Brahman's commands.

note.en: Hiranyaksha is named with Prahlada among the leading Daityas and Danavas of that age.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Santi Parva, Section CLXVI ('They were Hiranyakasipu, and Hiranyaksha, and Virochana, and Samvara, and Viprachitti, and Prahlada, and Namuchi, and Vali')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Santi Parva Section CLXVI names Hiranyaksha and Prahlada in the same roll of foremost Danavas.

note.en: Pulaha is one of the six mind-born sons of Brahma.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXV ('It is known that Brahman hath six spiritual sons, viz., Marichi, Atri, Angiras, Pulastya, Pulaha and Kratu')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXV names Pulaha among Brahman's six spiritual sons.

note.en: Kratu is one of the six mind-born sons of Brahma.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXV ('It is known that Brahman hath six spiritual sons, viz., Marichi, Atri, Angiras, Pulastya, Pulaha and Kratu')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXV names Kratu among Brahman's six spiritual sons.

note.en: Angiras is one of the six mind-born sons of Brahma.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXV ('It is known that Brahman hath six spiritual sons, viz., Marichi, Atri, Angiras, Pulastya, Pulaha and Kratu')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXV names Angiras among Brahman's six spiritual sons.

note.en: Pulaha and Kratu are named together among Brahma's six great Rishi sons.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXVI ('Marichi, Angiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, and Kratu -- these six great Rishis of great energy -- are the sons of Brahman')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXVI lists Pulaha and Kratu together as sons of Brahman.

note.en: Pulaha and Pulastya are both counted among Brahma's six mind-born Rishis.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXVI ('Marichi, Angiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, and Kratu -- these six great Rishis of great energy -- are the sons of Brahman')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXVI lists Pulastya and Pulaha together as sons of Brahman.

note.en: Kratu and Atri are both counted among Brahma's six mind-born Rishis.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXVI ('Marichi, Angiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, and Kratu -- these six great Rishis of great energy -- are the sons of Brahman')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXVI lists Atri and Kratu together as sons of Brahman.

note.en: Kratu and Angiras are both counted among Brahma's six mind-born Rishis.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXVI ('Marichi, Angiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, and Kratu -- these six great Rishis of great energy -- are the sons of Brahman')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXVI lists Angiras and Kratu together as sons of Brahman.

note.en: Pulaha and Angiras are both counted among Brahma's six mind-born Rishis.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXVI ('Marichi, Angiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, and Kratu -- these six great Rishis of great energy -- are the sons of Brahman')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXVI lists Angiras and Pulaha together as sons of Brahman.

note.en: Samvartta is one of Angiras's three sons.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXVI ('Angiras's sons are three, -- Vrihaspati, Utathya, and Samvarta, all of rigid vows')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXVI states Angiras's sons are three: Vrihaspati, Utathya and Samvarta.

note.en: Ashtavakra seeks Vadanya's daughter Suprabha in marriage, and Vadanya sends him north as a test.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Anusasana Parva, Section XIX ('Ashtavakra of severe penances, desirous of marriage, begged the high-souled Rishi Vadanya of his daughter. The name by which the damsel was known was Suprabha')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Anusasana Parva Section XIX has Ashtavakra beg the Rishi Vadanya for his daughter Suprabha; Section XXI calls Vadanya the father of his bride, not his teacher.

note.en: Ashtavakra wins entry to Janaka's sacrifice by out-arguing the gatekeeper and the king.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Tirtha-yatra Parva, Section CXXXIII ('Thereupon the king said, I give the privilege to enter. Do thou, therefore, go')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Sections CXXXII-CXXXIV narrate Ashtavakra going to king Janaka's sacrificial ground and disputing there.

note.en: Lomasa arrives among the exiled Pandavas and becomes Yudhishthira's guide on the tirtha pilgrimage.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Tirtha-yatra Parva, Section XCI ('there arrived at the spot the Rishi Lomasa of great energy... Yudhishthira the just enquired after the reason of his arrival')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section XCI narrates Lomasa's arrival and Yudhishthira receiving him and asking his errand.

note.en: Lomasa is foretold as the sage who will come to lead Yudhishthira through the tirthas.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Tirtha-yatra Parva, Section LXXXV ('a great Rishi of immeasurable energy, Lomasa by name, will come to thee. Do thou follow him')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section LXXXV has Yudhishthira told that the Rishi Lomasa will come and that he should follow him.

note.en: Lomasa arrives while the Pandava priest Dhaumya is describing the tirthas.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Tirtha-yatra Parva, Section XCI ('while Dhaumya was speaking thus, there arrived at the spot the Rishi Lomasa of great energy')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section XCI places Lomasa's arrival in the middle of Dhaumya's discourse to the Pandavas.

note.en: The royal sage Arshtishena instructs Yudhishthira on duty and on the Himalayan wonders.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Tirtha-yatra Parva, Section CLVIII ('Arshtishena said, During the Parvas sages subsisting on air and water come unto this best of the mountains')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CLVIII records Arshtishena's discourse answering Yudhishthira on the duties and the mountain.

note.en: Arshtishena's warning about the Yaksha realm frames Bhima's exploit on the Himalayan mountain.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Tirtha-yatra Parva, Section CLIX ('Surely, as Arshtishena said, the lord of wealth cometh thither')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CLIX recalls Arshtishena's words while recounting Bhimasena's deeds on the mountain.

note.en: The Pandavas with Draupadi come to Arshtishena's hermitage on the mountain.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Tirtha-yatra Parva, Section CLVII ('those valiant and warlike repressers of foes with Draupadi... saw the hermitage of the royal sage Arshtishena')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CLVII has the Pandavas with Draupadi reach the hermitage of the royal sage Arshtishena.

note.en: The Naga Karkotaka, cursed to immobility until Nala carries him, bites him and changes his form to Vahuka.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Nalopakhyana Parva, Section LXVI ('O king, that I am a snake, Karkotaka by name. I had deceived the great Rishi Narada... until one Nala taketh thee hence')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section LXVI has the snake name himself Karkotaka and tell Nala of the curse binding him until Nala bears him away.

note.en: Karkotaka's poison torments the possessing Kali until he leaves Nala, freeing him to return to Damayanti.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Nalopakhyana Parva, Section LXXII ('Kali came out of his body, incessantly vomiting from his mouth the virulent poison of Karkotaka')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section LXXII describes Kali leaving Nala while vomiting the poison of Karkotaka.

note.en: Richika is named the son of Bhrigu when he asks Gadhi for his daughter.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Tirtha-yatra Parva, Section CXV ('And Richika, the son of Bhrigu, asked for her to be united with himself in marriage')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CXV calls Richika the son of Bhrigu in the account of his marriage suit.

note.en: Richika wins Gadhi's daughter Satyavati by procuring the thousand steeds her father demanded.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Tirtha-yatra Parva, Section CXV ('in the city of Kanyakuvja, the daughter of Gadhi, Satyavati by name, was given in marriage... Richika... won a wife in the proper form')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CXV records Satyavati, daughter of Gadhi, given in marriage to Richika at Kanyakuvja.

note.en: Gadhi sets Richika the bride-price of a thousand steeds for his daughter's hand.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Tirtha-yatra Parva, Section CXV ('And then Gadhi spake to that Brahmana, who led a rigidly austere life, saying. There is a certain family custom in our race')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CXV narrates Gadhi's condition to Richika and Richika's promise of a thousand fleet steeds.

note.en: Jamadagni, father of Parashurama, is born to Richika and Satyavati.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Tirtha-yatra Parva, Section CXV ('Then she brought forth on the expected day a son by name Jamadagni. And this son of Bhrigu was endowed with both splendour and grace')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CXV has Satyavati bring forth Jamadagni, called a son of the Bhrigu line.

note.en: Richika appears in visible form to counsel his grandson Parashurama at Samantapanchaka.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Tirtha-yatra Parva, Section CXVII ('the mightiest scion of Bhrigu's race offered libations to his forefathers -- the Bhrigus, and Richika appeared to him in a visible form, and spake to him words of counsel')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CXVII has Richika appear before Jamadagni's son and speak words of counsel.

note.en: The Asura Naraka's soul is said to have taken the form of Karna, carrying his old enmity with Krishna into the war.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Section CCL ('The soul of the slain Naraka hath assumed the form of Karna. Recollecting his former hostility he will encounter both Kesava and Arjuna')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CCL states the soul of the slain Naraka assumed the form of Karna.

note.en: Naraka is the Asura slain by Krishna, whose remembered hostility passes into Karna.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Section CCL ('The soul of the slain Naraka hath assumed the form of Karna. Recollecting his former hostility he will encounter both Kesava and Arjuna')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CCL speaks of the slain Naraka whose former hostility to Kesava is carried into Karna.

note.en: Ila, who is turned to a woman in Uma's grove, is the son of the patriarch Kardama.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Uttara Kanda, Section C ('the graceful king Ila, the son of the patriarch Kardama, was highly pious')

verification.notes: Dutt's Uttara Kanda Section C twice names Ila the son of the patriarch Kardama.

note.en: Rama recounts Kardama's son Ila to Lakshmana in the Uttara Kanda.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Uttara Kanda, Section C ('I have heard, that formerly in the province of Valheeka, the graceful king Ila, the son of the patriarch Kardama, was highly pious')

verification.notes: Dutt's Uttara Kanda Section C has Rama himself relate the story of Kardama's son Ila to Lakshmana.

note.en: Pradyumna is named as Sanatkumara born among men in the Vrishni race.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXVII ('know that Pradyumna of great energy was Sanatkumara')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXVII states that Pradyumna of great energy was Sanatkumara.

note.en: Sanatkumara comes from Brahma's own region as an emissary of counsel.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXXV ('Sanatkumara came from the region of Brahman and gave him good counsel')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXXV places Sanatkumara as coming from the region of Brahman.
